{"decision":"RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL. Anthony is LEANING toward option (d) below as of 2026-07-30 — "I think I'm warming to this approach versus using git repos to capture the snapshot" — but has not said to promote it, so this stays a lean and not intent.

(d) GRAPH-ONLY, QUERIED RATHER THAN RENDERED. His words: "we could do this completely in the graph without git. We are just using git as a means to render a snapshot in time… it is reachable by 'what capabilities are due to be released in epoch 5' or 'what didn't we achieve that we were supposed to in increment 10?' and let the agent/user figure out how to render the snapshot."

WHY THIS IS STRONGER THAN THE FILE-PER-EPOCH RECOMMENDATION IT DISPLACES, and the displacement is a correction rather than a preference. Both things he named are QUESTIONS, not documents. A query answers them directly; a rendered file answers them only if someone rendered the right file at the right moment. And every materialised artifact needs a staleness check — `docs/design/reflow2.json` has one, `dataflow.html` has one, and `docs/loop-model.json` demonstrated the failure the same day by becoming permanently unreproducible. Not materialising is the only way to have no drift at all.

THE OBJECTION I RAISED AGAINST IT IS WEAKER THAN I THOUGHT, and this is the part worth correcting on the record. I argued that graph-only loses readability for someone not running reflow2 — a teammate, a reviewer, his brother — citing `req:design-reachable-without-the-repo`. But if the schedule lives in the graph, IT IS ALREADY IN THE COMMITTED EXPORT, which is in git on every commit. So the information is not unreachable; it is merely not pretty. Likewise "what did the plan say in March" is answerable today by `git log -p docs/design/reflow2.json` plus the export's own `prev_content_hash` chain. The file-per-epoch idea was therefore solving a problem the committed export already solves — adding an artifact to obtain a property that exists.

WHAT SURVIVES OF THE GIT IDEA, and it is narrower and better targeted. Git remains right where the thing being pinned actually LIVES in git: an ARRIVED epoch corresponds to real commits in real repos, and "what was actually deployed at epoch 3" is a question about the product. So the version-combination pin (`req:version-combination-is-an-object`) keeps its place on arrival. Forward-looking plans, which describe graph content, stay in the graph; backward-looking arrivals, which describe code, pin code.

A CONSEQUENCE WORTH NOTING FOR `req:graph-indexes-snapshots`. That requirement's stated intent is that "a user shouldn't have to remember which git branch a particular epoch or increment is in." Under (d) that is satisfied in the strongest possible way: there are no branches to remember, because nothing was put in one. The requirement's letter (index the snapshots) and its spirit (never make the user chase git) come apart here, and the spirit is the part he wrote it for.

RENDERING BECOMES AN OUTPUT, NOT A RECORD. "Let the agent/user figure out how to render the snapshot" is the right disposal: different consumers want different renderings — a markdown roadmap, a chart, a slide, a JSON feed — and choosing one file format now would be guessing on their behalf. `render_views.py` can emit an epoch view whenever asked, as a disposable projection.","name":"OPEN, but leaning — the schedule lives in the graph and is queried; nothing is snapshotted into git","rationale":"Anthony's idea and Anthony's lean, recorded as a lean. Nothing promoted: the brainstorm discipline is that an idea is not intent until he says so, and "warming to" is not "do it".

The correction to my own earlier recommendation is kept rather than tidied away. I had recommended file-per-epoch on main, and the reason it was wrong is instructive: the property I was reaching for — a git-visible history of the plan — already exists, because the schedule would live in the committed export and that file already has git history and its own lineage chain. Adding artifacts to obtain properties the design already has is the shape this project keeps finding, and it found it in my own advice this time.

The earlier wording of this node survives at `snap:epoch:wire-planning-cluster:dec:where-plans-live` and `:r2` — which are themselves the first production use of the second-revision-in-one-epoch fix landed on 2026-07-28.","status":"accepted"}
